deck_context.source_summary: Class 21 begins Week 5 and introduces AEM Multi-Site Management for traditional AEM Sites. It follows backend testing and prepares developers to trace content reuse and maintenance relationships with observable evidence.
deck_context.core_claim: MSM is predictable when a developer proves the source-to-Live-Copy relationship, identifies inherited versus local ownership and names the effective synchronization action before changing content.
canonical_facts: MSM reuses site content through maintained Live Copy relationships.
A similar path or identical rendering does not prove a Live Copy relationship.
A Live Copy source can be a regular page or a page referenced by a blueprint configuration.
A blueprint configuration identifies a source site and enables author-facing site creation and rollout capabilities.
A LiveRelationship connects a target resource to its source counterpart.
The language master is the primary authored source for a language.
Use MSM primarily within one language; translation manages changes across languages.
Component inheritance can be cancelled without cancelling inheritance for sibling components.
Re-enabling inheritance does not automatically synchronize content.
Synchronize begins on a Live Copy and pulls eligible source changes to that selected target.
Rollout begins on a blueprint source and pushes eligible changes to one or more Live Copies.
The effective rollout configuration determines the trigger and synchronization actions.
Standard rollout configuration runs on an explicit Rollout or Synchronize request.
Reset removes inheritance cancellations and restores source state, overwriting local changes.
Detach permanently removes the live relationship and is not reversible.
Live Copy Overview and Live Copy properties provide relationship and inheritance evidence.
revision_rules: Render exactly one fixed top-left eyebrow with the two-digit slide number and a short section label.
Use one clear visual model plus concrete evidence panels; do not fill slides with generic bullets alone.

Do not invent AEM paths, properties, rollout triggers or operations beyond the supplied context.

slides.title: Reuse requires a live relationship, not a similar path.
slides.intent: Establish the smallest truthful definition of MSM.
key_points: MSM reuses content through a maintained Live Copy relationship.
The source remains the origin for inherited content.
The Live Copy can receive later source changes.
A one-time copy is independent.
Prove origin and inheritance before comparing output.

local_context.required_background: Contrast SOURCE → LIVE RELATIONSHIP → LIVE COPY with SOURCE → ONE-TIME COPY. Identical pages can have different future behavior.

slides.title: Source, blueprint configuration and Live Copy are distinct objects.
slides.intent: Separate source content, configuration, target and per-resource relationship.
key_points: A Live Copy source is the page or branch that provides inherited content.
A blueprint configuration names a source site and enables site creation and rollout.
A Live Copy is the target branch.
A LiveRelationship connects equivalent resources.
A regular source is valid, but offers fewer authoring capabilities.

Same-language targets: /content/wknd/us/en and /content/wknd/ca/en
Keep each language in a separate relationship lane.

slides.title: Inheritance can stop at one component and continue elsewhere.
slides.intent: Show how a market takes local ownership of one component without disconnecting the page.
key_points: Pages and components inherit while live relationships remain active.
Cancel inheritance at the narrowest component that needs a local value.
Sibling components continue inheriting.
Re-enable restores inheritance but does not synchronize automatically.
Record who owns the exception and why.

slides.title: Inspect relationship evidence before changing content.
slides.intent: Give developers an evidence-first relationship trace.
key_points: Start from the Live Copy or source in the Sites console.
Inspect the Live Copy tab for source, inheritance and rollout configuration.
Use References → Live Copies → Live Copy Overview.
Check status at the exact page or component.
Paths and rendered equality are clues, not proof.

slides.title: Synchronize pulls one Live Copy; rollout pushes from the source.
slides.intent: Make direction, starting point and scope predictable.
key_points: Synchronize starts on a Live Copy and pulls eligible source changes.
Rollout starts on a blueprint source and pushes to one or more Live Copies.
Both use the effective rollout configuration.
Inheritance cancellation protects deliberate local values.
Name source, target, scope and expected result first.

slides.title: A rollout configuration defines trigger plus actions.
slides.intent: Explain enough configuration to predict behavior without teaching custom extensions.
key_points: Standard rollout configuration runs on explicit Rollout or Synchronize.
Actions can create, update, delete, reorder and update references.
Other configurations may trigger on activation, deactivation or modification.
On Modification can affect performance.
Customize only for a proven requirement.

local_context.required_background: Show TRIGGER → ROLLOUT CONFIGURATION → ACTION SET → TARGET RESULT. Standard: On Rollout with contentUpdate, contentCopy, contentDelete, referencesUpdate and orderChildren. Automatic trigger alternatives are guarded, not recommended defaults.

layout.composition: Horizontal contract pipeline with one primary standard path and a small alternatives rail.

constraints: Render On Rollout and the five standard action names exactly.

slides.title: Choose the least destructive relationship action.
slides.intent: Separate local ownership, temporary suspension, reset and permanent detachment.
key_points: Cancel/Re-enable: one local override, reversible.
Suspend/Resume: temporarily pause a page relationship.
Reset: remove cancellations and overwrite local changes with source state.
Detach: permanently remove the live relationship.
Preview scope and preserve evidence before Reset or Detach.

local_context.required_background: Compare Cancel/Re-enable, Suspend/Resume, Reset and Detach by granularity, reversibility, effect on local changes and future source updates. Reset and Detach require orange caution treatment.

layout.composition: Four-row decision matrix with a least-to-most-destructive progression and clear reversibility column.
layout.intent: Help authors stop at the smallest action that fits.

visual_elements.main_visual: Relationship-action matrix with reversibility and local-change impact.

constraints: Render Reset as overwriting local changes.
Render Detach as permanent and irreversible.
Do not imply Cancel Inheritance disconnects the entire page.

slides.title: MSM distributes content; translation changes language.
slides.intent: Prevent language problems from being diagnosed in the wrong subsystem.
key_points: MSM distributes translated source content within the same language.
Translation projects and connectors manage content across languages.
i18n dictionaries manage component-interface strings.
A market override is a content-ownership decision.
Diagnose relationship, translated content or UI dictionary first.

slides.title: Key takeaways
slides.intent: Consolidate five MSM decisions for Week 5 practice.
key_points: Prove the live relationship; do not infer it from matching content.
Separate source, blueprint configuration, Live Copy and LiveRelationship.
Cancel inheritance at the narrowest component that needs local ownership.
Predict trigger, direction, scope and action set before synchronization.
Keep MSM, translation and component i18n separate.
